title: First Visit, First Chart

patient.name: Mr Lim Wei Jie
patient.presenting_complaint: New patient referral from polyclinic for blurred vision when driving at night

history.hpc: Mr Lim is a 34-year-old new patient referred from a polyclinic for assessment of blurred distance vision, particularly when driving at night. He reports the blur has been gradual over the past 1-2 years. He wears glasses for distance but says his current pair 'feels weaker than before'. He has brought his current spectacles with him and is wearing them today.
history.pmhx: Myopia since age 12, last spectacle update was 3 years ago. No other ocular history. No diabetes, no hypertension.
history.family_hx: Mother has high myopia and wears thick glasses.
history.social_hx: Works long hours at a computer screen. Drives to work daily. Non-smoker.

va.right: 6/9 (LogMAR 0.18) with current glasses, improves to 6/6 with pinhole
va.left: 6/12 (LogMAR 0.3) with current glasses, improves to 6/6 with pinhole

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Not assessed at this stage — PSA role is VA measurement only
examination_findings.fundus: Not assessed — doctor to review after VA and refraction

logmar_va.method: Modified LogMAR (M&S System) chart, calibrated room distance, tested with current spectacles in place, right eye first by convention

diagnosis: Distance VA measured for both eyes with current correction. Both eyes improve to 6/6 with pinhole, suggesting an uncorrected or under-corrected refractive error rather than ocular pathology. Results recorded for doctor and refraction review.

immediate: Confirm patient's full name and NRIC against the registration record before starting
Perform hand hygiene and wipe the occluder with an alcohol wipe
Position Mr Lim comfortably facing the LogMAR chart at the calibrated distance
Confirm he is wearing his current spectacles for this test, as instructed
Test the right eye first — occlude the left eye and ask him to read all 5 letters per line from the top, left to right
Stop when he cannot read all 5 letters on a line and record the last completed line
Repeat the same procedure for the left eye, occluding the right eye
Since both eyes achieve 6/12 or better, apply the pinhole occluder to each eye in turn and re-test to see if vision improves
Wipe the occluder and pinhole with alcohol wipes and perform hand hygiene after the test
follow_up: Record both unaided-with-correction and pinhole results clearly in LogMAR notation in SCM
Hand the completed VA results to the doctor or technician performing refraction
Note that this is a new patient — flag that AR/AK and other new-patient investigations may also be required
patient_education: Inform Mr Lim that the vision test is complete and the doctor will review the results together with a refraction check
If he asks whether he needs new glasses, advise him that the doctor or optometrist will discuss this after refraction
Remind him to bring his current spectacles to all future visits for comparison

key_points: Confirms patient identity against the registration record before starting
Establishes that the patient is a new patient and notes the reason for referral
Confirms whether the patient is wearing current spectacles and tests with them in place
Notes relevant background (longstanding myopia, family history) without attempting to interpret it
Performs hand hygiene and wipes the occluder before and after the test
Tests the right eye first by convention, occluding the other eye correctly
Reads top-down, requiring all 5 letters correct before progressing to the next line
Applies pinhole correctly because vision is 6/12 or better in both eyes
Records results in correct LogMAR/Snellen notation with and without pinhole
Recognises that improvement with pinhole suggests a refractive (not pathological) cause
Does not tell the patient he needs new glasses or a new prescription
Identifies that this is a new patient and additional investigations may be needed
Defers interpretation of the result to the doctor or refractionist
Documents results accurately and completely in SCM
Hands results to the appropriate clinical staff for refraction
Communicates next steps to the patient without giving a diagnosis
Maintains a calm, professional, and welcoming manner appropriate for a first visit
